links.outcome: Agreement (ICC) between VideoLLM scores and expert ratings of dry eye video quality
links.effect: Across most metrics, VideoLLMs showed poor agreement with experts (ICC < 0.40); only PEMAT-A/V actionability reached ICC 0.50 (QwenVL) and 0.43 (InternVL).
links.quote: Across most metrics, VideoLLMs demonstrated poor agreement with expert annotations (ICC < 0.40), except for the actionability dimension of PEMAT-A/V, where QwenVL and InternVL achieved ICCs of 0.50 and 0.43, respectively, with the experts.

unlisted_practices: Using video LLMs to automatically assess quality and misinformation of online health videos

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the capability of video large language models (VideoLLMs) to automatically assess the quality and misinformation risks of patient-facing dry eye educational videos against expert clinician ratings.
